Their determinant is (1+5\lambda)(10\lambda-1), yielding eigenvalues -1/5 and 1/10. For -1/5, A=0 and y=Bx e^{-x}; for 1/10, A=-3B and y=C e^{x/2}(x-3). Each eigenfunction requires a nonzero scalar coefficient. These results agree with the captured Math Academy worked solution.

answers.ma_evidence: Thus, we have the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-\frac{1}{5}\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=\frac{1}{10}.$
So, the eigenfunctions corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively, are $Bx{e}^{-x}\text{ and }C{e}^{x/2}(x-3).$
